title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
gist: EPFL/Apple researchers find that, with equal time budget and the same frontier LLM backbone, open-source state-of-the-art autonomous ML engineering harnesses (multi-agent orchestrators, retrieval subagents) offer no advantage over a single session of a minimal read/write/bash coding agent. They conclude the backbone model drives performance and elaborate hand-crafted harnesses yield poor returns on current MLE benchmarks.

insights.claim: Under an equal time budget and the same frontier LLM backbone, open-source state-of-the-art MLE agent harnesses provide no advantage over a single session of a minimal-harness coding agent baseline.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Undercuts the defensibility of agent-scaffolding startups whose value proposition is elaborate orchestration around third-party models.
insights.quote: open-source state-of-the-art harnesses provide no advantages over a single session of a minimal-harness coding agent baseline
insights.locator: In this paper we find that

insights.claim: Large-scale systematic ablations indicate that machinery layers such as multi-agent orchestrators and retrieval subagents become redundant in the coding-agent setting.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Simpler agents mean lower engineering and inference overhead; value concentrates in the model layer.
insights.quote: we argue that the machinery layers become redundant in the coding agent setting

insights.claim: Effort spent elaborating hand-crafted harnesses around strong models yields poor returns on current MLE benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Capital and talent allocated to harness engineering may be misdirected relative to backbone model improvements.
insights.quote: the effort spent elaborating hand-crafted harnesses around strong models yields poor returns for current MLE benchmarks

insights.claim: The study points to the frontier LLM backbone, not the surrounding harness, as the primary driver of autonomous ML engineering agent performance.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Reinforces pricing power and moat of frontier model providers over application-layer agent wrappers.
insights.quote: pointing to the backbone as the primary driver for performance
insights.locator: In this paper we find that

insights.claim: Elaborate MLE agent harnesses arose because of progress stagnation over long-horizon cycles and limited LLM primitives, a rationale that weakens as models improve.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Scaffolding built to compensate for model weaknesses tends to be commoditized by each new model generation.
insights.quote: Often motivated by progress stagnation over long-horizon cycles and limited Large Language Model (LLM) primitives

insights.claim: Primitive but improved coding agents, where LLMs have direct access to the execution environment through read, write, and bash, have received little attention in the MLE agent field despite matching complex harnesses.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: General-purpose coding agents may absorb specialized vertical agent niches such as autonomous ML engineering.
insights.quote: where LLMs have direct access to the execution environment through read, write, and bash primitives—has received little attention in the field
